name: Gas station / convenience store
summary: Ground-up convenience store (≈2,500–6,500 SF) with fuel canopy, 4–8 multi-product dispensers (8–16 fueling positions) and 2–4 double-wall USTs on 1.5–5 acres. Because fuel system, canopy and a large paved fuel court ride on a small building, cost per store SF is high and swings with fueling positions. Evidence is moderate: one consultant development budget, eight 2025 Texas accessibility-registration estimates (self-reported, likely partial), and one 2024 public bid tab for UST/dispenser/canopy packages; no cost-consultant elemental data found.

typicalSize.method: Store SF: MMCG example 3,024 SF (g1); Texas 2025 registrations 3,600–7,773 SF (g2–g4, g6, g7, g9). Mid 4,500 SF; 8,500–10,900 SF registrations (g8, g10) treated as truck-stop/outliers or including canopy area.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Store SF per site acre. MMCG example 3,024 SF on 5.40 acres = 560 SF/ac (g1, large highway site). Typical suburban 4,500 SF store on 1.5–2.0 ac ≈ 2,200–3,000 SF/ac (judgment); urban corner 1 ac ≈ 3,500.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per store SF excluding pump positions; typical retail code 3–6 per 1,000 SF (judgment). Fueling positions not counted as parking.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Complete facility (store + canopy + fuel system + site) per store SF. MMCG budget: hard costs $3,169,000 for a 3,024 SF store with 8 fueling positions = $1,048/store SF (g1, 2025, includes canopy, tanks, site work). Texas 2025 registrations (whole gas station + c-store projects, self-reported): Dallas $3.0M / 7,773 SF = $386 (g7); Odessa $2.5M / 6,277 SF = $398 (g2); Palestine $2.0M / 5,210 SF = $384 (g4); Fort Worth $2.0M / 6,000 SF = $333 (g3); Houston $1.2M / 3,600 SF = $333 (g9); Houston $0.68M / 3,600 = $189 and $1.5M / 8,500 = $176 (g6, g8; likely partial). RSMeans 2019 basic convenience-store building only $126/SF ex-architect (g11; ≈$165–175 in 2025 before food-service and image upgrades). Built-up check for a 4,500 SF modern food-forward store: building ~$325/SF ($1.46M) + site work ~$0.7M + canopy ~$0.2M + fuel system ~$0.65M (g5 bid tab $332–552k for a smaller fleet system) ≈ $3.0M ≈ $670/SF. Mid $600 = between the TX registration cluster (~$385, Texas factor <1 and likely partial) and the built-up/MMCG figures. Low $350 = TX cluster; high $1,050 = MMCG.

scope.notes: Store building + fuel canopy + fuel system (USTs, piping, islands, dispensers, tank monitoring) + on-site work (fuel-court concrete, paving, storm/oil-water separator, utilities, lighting, landscaping). Excludes store equipment (coolers, shelving, food service, POS), signage/price pylon (ffe), land, soft costs, off-site/turn lanes, tap/impact fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (TX registrations, 350/600 → 0.6–0.65); premium ≈ large-format 'food-forward' c-store; luxury ≈ high/mid (MMCG, 1,050/600 = 1.75).

systemSplit.method: Built-up from the mid example (4,500 SF store, $3.0M): fuel system ≈ 22% (Div 11 dispensers 5% + Div 33 tanks/piping/utilities 15% + part of 26), canopy ≈ 6% (Div 13 pre-engineered canopy; g5 shows canopy ≈ 18–20% of the tank/dispenser package), site 31+32 ≈ 20% (large fuel-court concrete/paving), building ≈ 50% allocated with a small-retail pattern. Not from a published elemental estimate.

lineItems.name: Fuel system: double-wall USTs, product piping, islands, dispensers, tank monitoring

cost.method: Boone County, MO 2024 bid: 'Furnishing, delivery, and installation of new USTs, Islands, Dispensers, and FMUs' $331,570 (Sheriff site) and $551,995.97 (Road & Bridge site) (g5) — fleet-scale systems. Retail stations typically carry 3–4 tank compartments and 4–8 dispensers, so mid scaled ~1.2–2× the larger bid to $650k; high for 8 dispensers + diesel/DEF.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the baseline; scales mainly with number of dispensers and tanks.

lineItems.name: Fuel canopy (pre-engineered steel, LED lighting, fascia)

cost.method: Boone County 2024 bid canopy lines $68,777.38 and $101,930.00 (g5) for small fleet islands; retail 4–8 dispenser canopies are 2–4× larger in area → mid $200k (derived scaling).

lineItems.name: Removal of existing USTs, lines and contaminated soil (redevelopment sites)

cost.method: Boone County 2024 bid: removal of 6,000-gal UST $11,595 + 12,000-gal UST $24,550 + product lines/concrete $16,750 + contaminated soil up to 150 tons $36,475 = $89,370 (site 1); two 4,000-gal USTs $18,750 + lines $8,005 + soil $29,605 = $56,360 (site 2); soil beyond 150 tons $165/ton (g5). High allows larger soil volumes.

lineItems.notes: Only for rebuilds of existing stations.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Store equipment (walk-in cooler doors, reach-ins, shelving, food service, POS, security) + signage/price pylon. MMCG 'Equipment & Fixtures' $1,135,200 (g1) covers dispensers, tanks, POS, refrigeration, food service, signage; netting a ~$0.55–0.65M fuel system leaves ~$0.5–0.6M / 3,024 SF ≈ $165–200/SF (high end, food-forward). Low/mid for a basic store; derived — verify with an equipment vendor.

pctOfHard.method: MMCG soft costs $553,600 include contingency $316,900 and loan monitoring $35k → design/permits/other ≈ $200k on $3.169M hard ≈ 6.4% (g1). Add Phase I/II ESA, UST registration/permits, traffic study and legal → mid 10%.

softCosts.notes: Type-specific: environmental site assessments, state UST registration and tank-tightness testing, fuel-brand (jobber) image program costs, traffic/driveway permits (state DOT).

design.method: Judgment; fuel-court grading and DOT driveway design changes are common.

hard.method: MMCG contingency 'around 10% of hard construction costs' (g1); mid 8% with separate design contingency.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard $350–1,050/store SF × 1.07–1.15 soft ≈ $375–1,210; widened to $1,400 for small stores with many fueling positions (MMCG total excl. land/financing ≈ $4.86M / 3,024 SF incl. equipment ≈ $1,600, g1).

openQuestions: No sourced per-dispenser / per-tank retail costs (Toast and USDA pages returned 403); fuel-system and canopy carve-outs scale up a fleet bid — get a petroleum-equipment contractor quote.
Texas registration estimates are self-reported and probably understate full contract value; a few closed-out c-store GMPs (e.g., public P3 or travel-center bond documents) would help.
Brand image programs (e.g., large-format food-forward c-stores) can push building costs well above the mid.
